highlightAliases.old: Biopsychosocial Perspective: Addressing Personal, Social, and Environmental Contributions The experience of mobility disability can be viewed as mismatched personal capacities (physiologic and psychologic) and social and environmental demands.
highlightAliases.new: The experience of mobility disability can be viewed as mismatched personal capacities (physiologic and psychologic) and social and environmental demands.

highlightAliases.old: Prevalence The epidemiology of mobility disability can be considered from the perspective of basic or higher-level mobility.
highlightAliases.new: The epidemiology of mobility disability can be considered from the perspective of basic or higher-level mobility.

highlightAliases.old: Risk of Adverse Consequences Associated with Mobility Status Mobility problems have serious consequences.
highlightAliases.new: Risk of Adverse Consequences Associated with Mobility Status

highlightAliases.old: Care for the Immobile Person Interventions to reduce the consequences of immobility include determining the level of care need and living setting, training others to properly position and move the patient, implementing a mobilization plan, use of pressure-reducing devices to prevent pressure ulcer, and, sometimes, using equipment to aid in transfers (see Chapter 46).

highlightAliases.new: Biomechanical Perspective: Direct Assessment of the Body in Motion

highlightAliases.old: Attention to Factors That Modify Behavior and Environment The modifiable psychosocial factors that influence physical activity may offer opportunities to intervene (see Table 50-9).
highlightAliases.new: The modifiable psychosocial factors that influence physical activity may offer opportunities to intervene (see Table 50-9).

highlightAliases.old: Defining Mobility Mobility is the ability to move one’s own body through space.
highlightAliases.new: Mobility is the ability to move one’s own body through space.

highlightAliases.old: Classification Methods for Mobility Mobility classification is often driven by a tacit assumption of orderedness.
highlightAliases.new: Mobility classification is often driven by a tacit assumption of orderedness.

highlightAliases.old: Differential Diagnosis Based on a Physiologic Perspective A clinical schema for the comprehensive evaluation of mobility that is derived from Ferrucci, Tinetti, and the authors’ own work is proposed in Table 50-8.
highlightAliases.new: A clinical schema for the comprehensive evaluation of mobility that is derived from Ferrucci, Tinetti, and the authors’ own work is proposed in Table 50-8.

highlightAliases.old: Gait Speed as an Integrator of Multiple Approaches Walking is the foundation of mobility, is influenced by biomechanical and physiologic processes and environmental factors and is a major driver of disability.
highlightAliases.new: Walking is the foundation of mobility, is influenced by biomechanical and physiologic processes and environmental factors and is a major driver of disability.

highlightAliases.old: Biomedical Perspective: Using Organ System Impairment to Link Function and Disease The causes of mobility limitation can be assessed from a physiologic standpoint.
highlightAliases.new: The causes of mobility limitation can be assessed from a physiologic standpoint.

highlightAliases.old: Strategy for the Clinical Encounter There are no established standards for the overall evaluation and treatment of mobility problems in older adults.
highlightAliases.new: There are no established standards for the overall evaluation and treatment of mobility problems in older adults.

highlightAliases.old: Intervening Directly on Mobility Interventions directed at functional limitations are often rehabilitative in nature and involve exercise, adaptive equipment, and environmental modifications.
highlightAliases.new: Interventions directed at functional limitations are often rehabilitative in nature and involve exercise, adaptive equipment, and environmental modifications.

highlightAliases.old: Psychosocial and Environmental Assessment Mobility limitations are influenced by psychological, social, and environmental factors (Table 50-9).

highlightAliases.old: Clinical Assessment of Mobility Performance In ambulatory patients, simple assessment of gait speed is a useful place to start.
highlightAliases.new: In ambulatory patients, simple assessment of gait speed is a useful place to start.

highlightAliases.old: Treating Impairments Some impairments can be linked to diseases and pathologic processes that are amenable to medical treatment, and some impairments can be improved directly regardless of pathologic cause (see Table 50-8).
